thread.title: Susana Abaitua and Maxi Iglesias Star in Housing Satire Nuda Propiedad
thread.title_full: Susana Abaitua and Maxi Iglesias Star in Housing Satire Nuda Propiedad

author: Sofia Alvarez Entertainment Editor
title: Susana Abaitua and Maxi Iglesias Star in Housing Satire Nuda Propiedad
text:
Arriving in cinemas on October 2, 2026, the Spanish dark comedy Nuda propiedad stars Susana Abaitua and Maxi Iglesias as a couple forced into an unusual property purchase. Directed by Alberto Utrera, the film mirrors Spain’s severe housing crisis during real-world street protests.
Alberto Utrera Directs Housing Satire
Alberto Utrera directs the new feature Nuda propiedad, which arrives in Spanish theaters nationwide.
The plot centers on an ostensibly miraculous real estate deal: a spacious 110-square-meter apartment priced at 290,000 euros, secured through the legal arrangement of bare ownership where the elderly occupant retains the right to live there until death reported by Elpais. The project was conceived two years prior to its release, born from the filmmakers’ own frustrations with soaring rental costs and tightening credit.
Rather than framing the narrative as a dry social drama, the creative team opted for a biting dark comedy that weaves in elements of suspense, touching upon tones reminiscent of Hitchcock’s Rear Window and Woody Allen’s Manhattan Murder Mystery according to Fotogramas.
Susana Abaitua and Maxi Iglesias Transform for Film
Maxi Iglesias embraced a less glamorous persona to play Lucas, deliberately moving away from the romantic lead parts that defined much of his earlier career noted SensaCine. When the script arrived, I loved it, Iglesias shared during a promotional appearance, noting his desire to shed standard casting expectations as detailed by SensaCine.
To physically embody the mathematics teacher, Iglesias altered his daily regimen, attempting to gain weight and requesting a more unkempt appearance.
Susana Abaitua portrays Vera, a post office worker whose drive to secure a permanent home is compounded by personal doubt and the search for stability alongside her partner near their forties.
Protests Collide With Cinema Release
During the opening quarter of the year, housing costs in Spain climbed 12.8% year-over-year—more than double the European Union average—while standard rentals consumed half of the average gross salary in the prior year reported ABC.
The theatrical rollout aligns with widespread public demonstrations over housing affordability across major Spanish cities noted ABC. Cast members have pointed out the eerie synchronicity between the film’s fiction and ongoing street protests according to ABC.
Pepe Viyuela noted, Coincidence shows the connection that cinema has with reality,
according to El Confidencial.
For younger demographics, securing independent housing demands nearly all net earnings, keeping emancipation rates low as individuals are frequently forced to share accommodations simply to split expenses rather than out of romance according to ABC.
Critics Review Utrera’s Feature
Produced by Garojay Producciones in association with Buendía Estudios, the 99-minute feature relies on word-of-mouth momentum to find its audience in theaters reported Latidosporelcine.
Critics note clear thematic debts to foundational works of Spanish social satire. Utrera’s film updates that despair for a modern era defined by real estate speculation, investment funds, and aggressive property agencies noted Best Movie España.
As audiences fill seats while demonstrations continue outside cinemas, the film leaves viewers confronting the bitter reality of trying to find stability in an inaccessible market noted Best Movie España.
